addition_3_truncation_diagnostic.rationale: CoT generations are longer while max_new_tokens stays 768. Without a cap-hit readout, a degraded CoT+alpha result cannot be separated into a commitment change and a length truncation.
addition_3_truncation_diagnostic.metric: cap_hit_rate = fraction of samples whose re-tokenized generation reaches the generation cap
addition_3_truncation_diagnostic.why_not_exact: The stored text is re-tokenized offline, so the boundary is approximate: on llama a=0, '>=768' reads 82.0% while '>=767' reads 94.0% and '>=760' reads 94.3%. The plateau above 760 is the real cap population; an exact-equality test undercounts it by ~12 percentage points.
addition_3_truncation_diagnostic.status: secondary diagnostic, NOT a primary metric and NOT in any Holm family

measured_on_the_already_unsealed_no_cot_.status: EXPLORATORY (post-unseal), recorded here because it bounds how the existing Llama commitment numbers may be read
measured_on_the_already_unsealed_no_cot_.consequence: Llama's GSM-Hard generations hit the cap in 91-96% of samples in EVERY cell, with a median decode length of exactly 768. So Llama's chars-median and post-commit-share in AdaptiveThinking.md 5.10.1 are measured on truncated generations and must be cited with that caveat. Qwen is far less affected (13-23%). This does NOT invalidate the P3 accuracy comparison, which is paired per question under one identical convention across all cells.
measured_on_the_already_unsealed_no_cot_.consequence_for_cot: Llama CoT is expected to be at or above this cap rate. If Llama's CoT dAcc is null or negative, truncation is a live alternative explanation and must be reported alongside the commitment reading rather than being resolved in favour of either.
